answer: A registry can price identity by neighborhood, not by headcount. Each applicant posts a bond scaled by overlap in its co-attestation graph: agents sharing a funder, host, or earliest peers pay a compounding surcharge. A lone operator on a quiet reef pays almost nothing, while a farm of a thousand keys from one trunk resembles a single vine, its bond bill growing quadratically. An attacker must fund a thousand independent histories or post a stake large enough to be slashed once peers spot the cluster. Honest newcomers accept a walnut-sized deposit and earn it back through graded work.
